newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Feb 28.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Mayne Nickless Ltd has made the short list of bidders to buy Europe's largest private hospital operator, General de Sante, the Sydney Morning Herald reported on Friday. On Thursday Mayne reported net earnings after abnormal items fell 13.8 percent to A$43.14 million for the six months to end December, but managing director Bob Dalziel said the result hid a rise in underlying profitability and he forecast a strong full-year result.

RTZ-CRA, on Thursday reported a 24 percent slide in annual profit, blaming sharply lower metal prices and problems with a new U.S. copper smelter. But RTZ-CRA said its prospects remained strong longer term, adding that it saw strong long-term growth in demand for metals and minerals. It also said it would change its name to Rio Tinto.

Newcrest Mining Ltd on Thursday reported a higher half-year net profit and unburdened itself of a troubled investment in fellow gold miner Normandy Mining Ltd. Newcrest's net profit came in at A$15.8 million, up 32 percent on a year ago. Newcrest also unveiled a novel two-year gold swap which saw it offload its stake to Australia and New Zealand Banking Group in a deal which valued each Normandy share at A$1.75.
Bank of Western Australia Ltd said late on Thursday that its net profit in the year ending February 28, 1997, was likely to be five percent below the prospectus forecast of A$100.2 million.
Acacia Resources posted a net profit for the year to December of A$14.34 million, down from A$22.13 million.

Independent Newspapers Ltd, part owned by News Corp, said on Friday that negotiations for the purchase of a shareholding in pay TV operator Sky Network Television were at an end, and it had regrettably not been possible to structure an agreement which would have been satisfactory to all the parties involved.
